question: Lamb and cardigan: how the knit reads against natural fleece, and how she carries the tally stick and bell.

options.label: A
options.name: Crook-staff drover: fitted berry knit, fleece under the hem, bell on the crook
options.question: The tally stick is a tall notched crook-staff; the fold bell hangs on its hook.
parts: staff (timber, brass bell on berry cord): layer 0 in E (far hoof), 5 in S/W; hand; swings in walk, raised in cheer, a guard bar in fight
legs x2 (plaster, timber hooves): layer 1; hip; 6-frame swing, tuck in hop and nap
fleece hem (snow curls): layer 2; hip; bobs 1 px a step
cardigan torso (berry knit, rib hem, brass buttons): layer 3; hip; breath 1 px
sleeves x2 (berry, timber hooves): far 1 tone back, layer 2/4; chest; swing, wind-up, cast
head (plaster face, ears, snow crown): layer 6; chest; tilts in fidget, ears droop in nap
ears x2 (plaster, berry inner): layer 5; head; flop on hop and hit
options.pose: Stands square by her staff like a shepherd on watch, chin up, already counting the dusk.
notes: Works: the tall crook gives the cast its only vertical prop line, so she reads at 2 px even beside Tam and Puffcap.
Knit vs fleece: knit rows of 2 px dashes in berry, curls in snow at the crown, chest V and under the hem.
Risk: the staff doubles the cell width in fights and walk frames; E holds it behind, W at her back.
Compared with Eastward 05 (curly-haired woman, Sam): curls as 4-6 px lobes with lit caps, 3 tones a lobe.

options.label: B
options.name: Collar-bell puffball: black-faced lamb, cropped sky knit, round fleece belly
options.question: A short tally stick tucked in a strap at her hip; the bell on a collar ribbon at her throat.
parts: legs x2 (slate, thin, slate hooves): layer 1; hip; quick 6-frame trot, tucked in nap
fleece belly (snow curls, timber strap, brass buckle): layer 2; hip; squash 1 px on hop
tally stick (timber): layer 1 in E, 3 in S/W; hip strap; jiggles on walk, drawn as a blade in strike
bolero (sky knit, rib edge): layer 3; chest; breath
sleeves x2 (sky, slate hooves): layer 2/4; chest; count, wind-up, guard
bell (brass, sky ribbon): layer 5; chest; swings a step behind the body, rings in fidget and cast
head (slate face, pale lower eye rims, slate ears, snow crown): layer 6; chest
options.pose: A round, busy little lamb, hooves together, ready to trot off after a stray.
notes: Works: the black face and legs against a white puffball read in two values at any size, and nobody else is round.
Knit vs fleece: the knit is only a short sky bolero, so most of the body is fleece; the two meet in one clear line.
Risk: on a black face the eyes need a pale lower rim and glint to read; the stick at the hip is small and hides in E.
Compared with Eastward 05: the curly-haired woman's hair mass, here scaled to the whole belly.

options.label: C
options.name: Big-cardigan clerk: oversized clay knit to the knees, stick behind the ear
options.question: The tally stick rides behind her ear like a pencil; the brass fold bell hangs on a cord from her pocket.
parts: legs x2 (plaster stubs, timber hooves): layer 1; hip; short steps, the hem hides most of the swing
cardigan coat (clay knit, brass buttons, patch pockets): layer 2; hip; the hem sways 1 px after each step
bell (brass, on a timber cord from the pocket): layer 3; hip; swings and settles a frame late
sleeves x2 (clay, rolled rib cuffs, timber hooves): layer 2/4; chest; flap in cheer and cast
tally stick (timber): behind the ear, layer 5 (W), 0 (E); head; comes to the hoof in fidget and cast
head (plaster face, ears, snow crown): layer 6; chest
options.pose: Swamped in a hand-me-down cardigan, sleeves rolled, a fussy little clerk of the flock.
notes: Works: the A-line coat makes a triangle no other folk has, and the big brass buttons and pockets read at 2 px.
Knit vs fleece: a lot of knit, so the knit rows carry the material; fleece shows at the crown and the chest.
Risk: legs vanish under the hem, so the walk leans on the hem sway; clay knit must stay apart from Bramble's fox-clay fur.
Compared with Eastward 05: the woman in the purple cardigan (buttons, a placket line and a hem row at this height).

final.name: Collar-bell puffball (final): black-faced lamb, round berry cardigan, stick behind the ear
grafts: From C: the tally stick tucked behind her left ear like a pencil, anchored to the head in every facing; it comes to the hoof only for the fidget and the cast.
From C: a real cardigan, round over the fleece, to mid-thigh, open down the front with a button band (three brass buttons) and a ribbed hem.
Cast-wide: the knit moves from sky (Bramble's) to berry, drawn as rib columns.
Eyes on the black face: ink 3 x 2 (2 x 2 in profile), a 2 px glint, a pale lower lid, a berry blush.
Kept from B: the collar bell at her throat, the round fleece silhouette, the thin slate legs.
parts: familiar perch: back shoulder (E: x smaller, W: x larger), behind the head; layer 0; chest
far leg / far sleeve (slate / berry, a tone back): layer 1; hip / chest; all facings
near leg (slate, thin, slate hoof): layer 2; hip; 6-frame trot, tucked in hop and nap, forward in sit
cardigan body (berry rib, open front, brass buttons, rib hem) over the fleece belly (snow curls): layer 3; hip; breath 1 px, squash 1 px on hop; the opening moves to the front edge in E/W
head (slate face, pale lower lids, berry blush, slate ears, snow crown): layer 4; chest; leads the strike (a headbutt), tilts in the fidget, ears lift on hit and cheer
tally stick (timber, notched): layer 3.5 behind the LEFT ear (S: screen right; E: behind the head; W: over the near ear); head; to the near hoof in fidget and cast
collar bell (brass on a timber strap): layer 5; chest; a free pendulum a frame behind the body, rings in fidget and cast
near sleeve (berry rib, slate hoof): layer 6; chest; swing, guard, reach, raise
final.pose: A round, busy little lamb, hooves at her sides, ready to trot off after a stray; she headbutts in a fight.
notes: Compared side by side with Eastward 05 at the same height: the curly-haired woman (curls as lobes with a lit cap and dark crescent) and the woman in the purple cardigan (placket, buttons, hem row).
Works: the black face and legs against a white crown and a round berry body read in two values; nobody else in the cast is round, and the stick on the head reads in every facing.
Strike is a headbutt (head leads, hooves back): sheep-like and keeps the stick out of the swing.
Open: whether the stick should also come to the hoof for strike, and the bell's ring effect frames.
